item: Hotels and hotel rooms in Lower Manhattan
then_quote:
Lower Manhattan has 18 hotels and 4,092 
hotel rooms. This is triple the number of 
hotels and 78% more hotel rooms than 
were open in 2001, despite the loss of the 
825-room Vista Hotel at 3 World Trade 
Center on 9/11.
now_quote: The current hotel inventory for the neighborhood stands at 8,100 rooms across 42 hotels.
notes: 2001 hotel count is derived from the Downtown Alliance's 'triple' statement (18/3 = 6) and the 2001 room count from '78% more' (4,092/1.78 = ~2,299); the Alliance never prints the raw 2001 numbers on the pages fetched. Six hotels in 2001 is stated outright by NY1 (news fallback, https://ny1.com/nyc/all-boroughs/9-11-20-years-later/2021/09/09/how-lower-manhattan-has-evolved-since-9-11): 'Hotels are popping up, too. In 2001, there were only six in Lower Manhattan. Now, there are 37.' SOLM 2011 also: 'Visitors can now stay in one of 18 Lower Manhattan hotels—triple the number that existed on September 10, 2001.' The Q2 2026 hotel inventory PDF (https://downtownny.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Hotel-Inventory-Q1-2026-Sheet4.pdf) lists 47 rows including 3 closed Sonder properties and totals 'Total Existing: 8,100 42'; the count peaked at 44 hotels / 8,534 rooms in Q1 2025 per the fact sheet. Fact sheet also: 'Hotel Occupancy Rate 88%'.

notes: Inventory definitions are inconsistent across sources, so treat the 110M figure with care: SOLM 2011 cover lists '86,372,000 SQUARE FEET OF OFFICE SPACE' in 2011 after 'the loss of 13.4 million square feet of office space' (which implies ~100M in 2001 for the south-of-Chambers area), while the OSC/Assembly 2005 report says the downtown (south of Canal) inventory fell 'from 92.9 million square feet to 90.6 million square feet' between 2003 and 2004. The safest framing: roughly 100M+ sq ft before 9/11 vs ~82M today, with conversions (not just 9/11) driving the shrinkage.

item: Total visitors to the 9/11 Memorial and Museum
now_value: Memorial: more than 83 million since 2011; Museum: over 24 million since 2014. In 2025 alone: 11.3 million Memorial, 2.4 million Museum
now_quote:
More than 83 million people who visited the Memorial from across the U.S. and around the world since its dedication on September 11, 2011.
Over 24 million people who visited the Museum since it opened to the public in May 2014.
notes: The financial-legal page does not state its as-of date. Annual figures: 2025 annual report (https://911memorial.org/2025-annual-report): 'We are profoundly grateful to the 9/11 community members, supporters, 2.4 million Museum visitors and 11.3 million Memorial visitors who came to our site to remember, reflect, and learn.' 2024 annual report (https://www.911memorial.org/2024-annual-report): 'We were privileged to welcome 2.4 million visitors to the Museum and 11.6 million to the Memorial.' Earlier checkpoints: 911memorial.org blog (2017): 'More than 10 million people have visited the 9/11 Memorial Museum since it opened in May 2014' and 'The accompanying 9/11 Memorial has had more than 33 million visitors since it opened in September 2011.' OSC 2016: 'As of 2015, more than 23 million tourists had visited the National September 11 Memorial and 4 million had visited the Memorial Museum.'
